2026-08-30 batch E1 (the SyncPlay push differential): the 21 "verified-by-push-probe" records are DELETED, not amended. GET /Albums/{itemId}/Similar.classification: flat-provider methodology (SET-GATED, order not gateable). Seeds of this kind take the C# FLAT provider: one `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags, IncludeItemTypes = [<kind>], EnableGroupByMetadataKey = false, EnableTotalRecordCount = true, OrderBy = [(ItemSortBy.Random, SortOrder.Ascending)] }` — identical in v10.11.8 (built inline at LibraryController.cs:791-801) and in master (SeriesSimilarItemsProvider.cs:49, MusicAlbumSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, AudioSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, LiveTvProgramSimilarItemsProvider.cs:89). Ferrofin runs the same query and, as of this pass, the same `Random` order. IT BRIEFLY DID NOT: batch A2 first shipped `SortName` here, which is not cosmetic — at limit < |candidates| a fixed order returns a DIFFERENT ITEM, measured on the loop pair as `/Items/{audio}/Similar?limit=1` answering 'Artist 01 Album 01 Track 02' on five consecutive Ferrofin calls while Jellyfin alternated Track 02 / Track 03. That divergence is now closed in the server (`similar_items_manager.rs::flat_similar`, unit test `the_flat_provider_orders_random_not_by_name`), not papered over. WHAT THIS LEDGER ROW DOES AND DOES NOT GATE: `Random` on both sides means the ORDER can never be diffed by any probe, and neither can a page narrower than the candidate pool — parity_diff aligns arrays by Path>Name>Id, so a reordered Items array returns 0 diffs and always will. The reads.py leg therefore pins `limit=1000`, far above the fixture's pool, where the answer is the whole candidate set and so fully determined; what is gated there is the SET, TotalRecordCount and every per-item DTO field. Anything order-sensitive is covered by unit tests instead, never by this row. GREEN BUT VACUOUS ON THE CURRENT FIXTURE — read this row as 'no divergence detected', not as 'verified'. `suite/perf/gen-fixtures.sh` gave each of the 3 albums a UNIQUE music genre, so the candidate universe is empty by construction on BOTH servers and the leg diffs `{"Items": [], "TotalRecordCount": 0}` against itself. The fixture is changed (two of the three artists now share a genre) but that only takes effect at the campaign's final wipe-and-provision; until that sweep runs, the album matching itself is covered by the `an_album_seed_matches_albums_sharing_a_genre_only` unit test (two albums sharing a genre, a same-genre track that must NOT come back because IncludeItemTypes is [MusicAlbum] alone, and the ExcludeArtistIds leg with a positive control). A real Ferrofin bug found behind this row IS fixed and verified live: album Genres/Studios/PremiereDate are inherited from the album's Audio children (C# AlbumMetadataService + MetadataService.UpdateGenres/UpdateStudios/UpdatePremiereDate); Ferrofin aggregated only album-artist and year, so every album had `Genres: []` and was unreachable by the Genres= query this endpoint issues. After the fix, F album Genres/PremiereDate/ProductionYear match J exactly (Jazz/Rock/Ambient, 2022-01-01T00:00:00.0000000Z, 2022).

GET /Artists.classification:
jellyfin-bug (RunTimeTicks / CumulativeRunTimeTicks ONLY; every other leg of this row now diffs clean by measurement). `MusicArtistResolver` is PORTED (library_scan.rs::plan_music_node + is_music_artist, a port of v10.11.8 Emby.Server.Implementations/Library/Resolvers/Audio/MusicArtistResolver.cs:54-125), so an artist directory now resolves to a real MusicArtist row parented into the music library, on Jellyfin's OWN path-derived id (measured byte-identical on the fixture: Artist 01 = 0f39932400340734bea41ffc13aaddc4, Artist 02 = 2b3868bfaa266cc1d3cc4c3dd5d40800, Artist 03 = 697d2b7b6ec56d3cf7e87c2de748b0cd), with its albums re-parented onto it. That closed Path, CanDelete, RecursiveItemCount and the empty user-scoped MusicArtist universe.

WHAT REMAINS, and why it is Jellyfin's bug and not Ferrofin's: with the artist resolved as a folder, `MetadataService.UpdateCumulativeRunTimeTicks` (MediaBrowser.Providers/Manager/MetadataService.cs:451) sums the RunTimeTicks of the non-folder children returned by `GetChildrenForMetadataUpdates`. For a MusicArtist that method is OVERRIDDEN — `ArtistMetadataService.GetChildrenForMetadataUpdates` (MediaBrowser.Providers/Music/ArtistMetadataService.cs:44-56) returns `item.IsAccessedByName ? item.GetTaggedItems(Recursive, IsFolder=false) : item.GetRecursiveChildren(i => i is IHasArtist && !i.IsFolder)`, NOT the base class's plain `folder.GetRecursiveChildren()` at MetadataService.cs:397-401. A folder-resolved artist takes the second arm, and `Audio : IHasArtist`, so the set is exactly the three tracks — the override strengthens the conclusion rather than changing it, and it is cited here because re-deriving the number from the base method lands on the wrong call. `MusicArtist.SupportsCumulativeRunTimeTicks => true` (MusicArtist.cs:38). 3 tracks x 20000000 = 60000000, which is what Ferrofin stores. The 10.11.8 oracle stores 0, and its OWN DateLastRefreshed timestamps show why — a first-scan ordering race, read out of this lab's /config/data/jellyfin.db:
  MusicArtist 'Artist 01'   RunTimeTicks 0         DateLastRefreshed 2026-08-30 00:29:30.8359533
  Audio       'Track 01'    RunTimeTicks 20000000                    2026-08-30 00:29:30.8815808
  Audio       'Track 02'    RunTimeTicks 20000000                    2026-08-30 00:29:30.8973703
  Audio       'Track 03'    RunTimeTicks 20000000                    2026-08-30 00:29:30.9096119
  MusicAlbum  'Album 01'    RunTimeTicks 60000000                    2026-08-30 00:29:30.9187306
The artist refreshed 46 ms BEFORE its first track was probed, so it summed a set of NULLs. The album — identical code, `SupportsCumulativeRunTimeTicks` also true, refreshed after all three — got the right number. A rescan does not repair it either: `UpdateMetadataFromChildren` is gated on `isFullRefresh || currentUpdateType > None`. Matching Jellyfin here would mean reproducing a first-scan race on purpose.

Until ratified the row stays deep_verified=false against this oracle, honestly — the divergence is REAL and visible, not hidden. parity_diff.VOLATILE was NOT widened for RunTimeTicks and must not be.

GET /Audio/{itemId}/RemoteSearch/Lyrics.classification: expected-extension: Jellyfin 10.11.8 ships NO ILyricProvider implementation — `git grep ": ILyricProvider" v10.11.8 -- '*.cs'` returns nothing (only the interface, LyricManager and the CoreAppHost DI scan), and that server's own GET /Libraries/AvailableOptions reports `LyricFetchers: []`. Ferrofin compiles LrcLib in the way it compiles TMDB in. On this fixture both answer `200 []` — Jellyfin structurally, Ferrofin because the synthetic titles ("Artist 01 Album 01 Track 01") match no lrclib record (egress verified: `curl https://lrclib.net/api/search` returns 200 from BOTH containers, so this is a corpus fact, not a network gap). The row therefore agrees on an empty list and compares nothing; only a real-track fixture would give it content, and then only Ferrofin could return any.

GET /MusicGenres.classification:
open-work (NOT accepted) — SUPERSEDES "verified 2026-08-11: QueryResult<BaseItemDto>, status+schema conformant", which was a shape check, and CORRECTS batch B1's first-round residual that blamed the diff on lab damage. A `MusicGenre` row that carries no music items lists on Jellyfin and does not list on Ferrofin. Proof it is behavioural, not drift: after the `CreateItemByName` port BOTH servers hold a lazily created MusicGenre "Action" row (/MusicGenres/Action is 200 with an Id on both), yet /MusicGenres lists it only on Jellyfin (J: Action/Ambient/Jazz/Rock, H: Ambient/Jazz/Rock). C# has no owner-type restriction here: `BaseItemRepository.ByName.cs:44-52` implements BOTH `GetGenres` and `GetMusicGenres` as `GetItemValues(filter, _getGenreValueTypes, <"Genre"|"MusicGenre">)` — the only difference is the by-name item TYPE looked up; the split by owner type exists solely on the *Names* variants (ByName.cs:56-82). Ferrofin's `item_repository::get_music_genres` passes the music types as `with_item_types` and `get_genres` passes them as `exclude_item_types`, a COMPENSATING restriction for a different divergence: Ferrofin's scan creates a `Genre` row for every genre value including music ones, where Jellyfin's validators split them. Un-defer path, and the order matters: fix the scanner so a music-only genre value materializes a `MusicGenre` row and not a `Genre` row, THEN drop both compensating restrictions, THEN re-verify `GET /Genres` (deep-verified today, and it would go red if the restriction were dropped alone). Needs a scan-path change plus its own perf gate, so it is named here as open work, not carried as accepted.

That committed number was taken on a DIFFERENT pair on 2026-08-29 and is not a before-measurement of this one, so 'unchanged' was asserted without a basis. The new EXTRAs are Comedy/Drama/SciFi/Thriller, from the `/MusicGenres?userId=..&includeItemTypes=Movie` leg (reads.py:680), where Ferrofin answers 5 and Jellyfin answers 1.

It is NOT a regression the batch caused, and that is established by evidence rather than by assertion. Comparing this lane's Ferrofin database before the batch's rebuild (copy taken 12:08 local, before commit f64dda9) against it now: the Genre/MusicGenre `BaseItems` rows are byte-identical (10 MusicGenre + 9 Genre, same names, same DateCreated — the four MusicGenre rows Comedy/Drama/SciFi/Thriller were created at 2026-08-30T02:37:28Z by reads.py's own deliberate by-name write leg, ~11 h before the rebuild), and the `ItemValues`/`ItemValuesMap` counts for every one of those genre values are byte-identical too (action 201, comedy 202, drama 202, scifi 201, thriller 202, ambient/jazz/rock 4). f64dda9 also does not touch `item_repository.rs` or the genres handler at all. Seeds of this kind take the C# FLAT provider: one `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags, IncludeItemTypes = [<kind>], EnableGroupByMetadataKey = false, EnableTotalRecordCount = true, OrderBy = [(ItemSortBy.Random, SortOrder.Ascending)] }` — identical in v10.11.8 (built inline at LibraryController.cs:791-801) and in master (SeriesSimilarItemsProvider.cs:49, MusicAlbumSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, MusicArtistSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, AudioSimilarItemsProvider.cs:50, LiveTvProgramSimilarItemsProvider.cs:89). Ferrofin runs the same query and, as of this pass, the same `Random` order. IT BRIEFLY DID NOT: batch A2 first shipped `SortName` here, which is not cosmetic — at limit < |candidates| a fixed order returns a DIFFERENT ITEM, measured on the loop pair as `/Items/{audio}/Similar?limit=1` answering 'Artist 01 Album 01 Track 02' on five consecutive Ferrofin calls while Jellyfin alternated Track 02 / Track 03. That divergence is now closed in the server (`similar_items_manager.rs::flat_similar`, unit test `the_flat_provider_orders_random_not_by_name`), not papered over. WHAT THIS LEDGER ROW DOES AND DOES NOT GATE: `Random` on both sides means the ORDER can never be diffed by any probe, and neither can a page narrower than the candidate pool — parity_diff aligns arrays by Path>Name>Id, so a reordered Items array returns 0 diffs and always will. The reads.py leg therefore pins `limit=1000`, far above the fixture's pool, where the answer is the whole candidate set and so fully determined; what is gated there is the SET, TotalRecordCount and every per-item DTO field. Anything order-sensitive is covered by unit tests instead, never by this row. SERIES SEED: the pre-A2 server ran the weighted MOVIE scorer for every kind, which credits a shared studio (+5) and shared people and pulled genre-unrelated series in (F ['Series 06','Series 03','Series 05','Series 07'] vs J ['Series 06']); `SeriesSimilarItemsProvider` filters on Genres/Tags alone, and porting it made the set match. The probe also exposed a DTO gap since fixed: Ferrofin omitted `AirDays` on Series where 10.11.8 always sends `[]` (v10.11.8 DtoService.cs:1243 assigns `series.AirDays`, and v10.11.8 Series.cs:31 initialises it to `Array.Empty<DayOfWeek>()` while no column persists it) — the null-where-Jellyfin-sends-non-null shape strict clients crash on.

GET /Trailers/{itemId}/Similar.classification: instance/methodology (PROPERTY-VERIFIED, NOT body-diffed — the ledger counts and lists this row separately from the deep-verified ones; status codes, the empty short-circuits, the count invariant and the candidate rule are what is gated, by the reads.py `similar_invariants` probe, and each of the three property rows now issues its OWN alias rather than all three probing /Movies). (2) ALGORITHM: 10.11.8 builds ONE flat `InternalItemsQuery { Genres = item.Genres, Tags = item.Tags }`, while Ferrofin ports upstream master's weighted `MovieSimilarItemsProvider` (genre 10 / tag 5 / studio 5 / director 50 / actor+guest-star 15, MovieSimilarItemsProvider.cs:27-31) plus its phase-2 `IsMovie = true, IsPlayed = false` + ConfigureUserAccess pass. The engineering case for keeping master is the repo's 'do not port Jellyfin bugs' rule — 10.11.8 additionally over-returns by 4 at every limit (measured 1/3/5/12/50 -> 5/7/9/16/54) because `BaseItemRepository.PrepareFilterQuery` (v10.11.8:1427-1430) adds 4 when `EnableGroupByMetadataKey` and never trims back, while Ferrofin honours limit exactly as master's `.Take(requestedLimit)` does — but the call is the owner's, and reverting to 10.11.8's flat query would make these three rows body-diffable at a pinned wide limit. *** WHAT IS VERIFIED LIVE instead of a body diff (every fact computed per server and then compared): status 200, StartIndex 0, TotalRecordCount == len(Items), the seed is never returned, every Type is in the C# IncludeItemTypes, the page is full, len(Items) <= limit+4 (the named Jellyfin quirk is the ONLY slack), an unknown seed is 404 on both, a nil seed is 200-empty on both, an Episode seed short-circuits empty on both, the five aliases agree as sets at limit=1000, and `obeys_own_candidate_rule` — each server's answer is re-derived independently from the DTO fields under ITS OWN documented algorithm (Jellyfin: every row shares a genre or tag with the seed, which 200 of the 500 fixture movies violate; Ferrofin: the answer equals master's weighted model's top-N IN ORDER by score desc, then Ferrofin's OWN SortName/Id tiebreak — master has no tiebreak at all, `MovieSimilarItemsProvider.cs:189-195` is `OrderByDescending(score)` alone, so that clause pins Ferrofin's rule, which is strictly more determined than the C#'s). POST /Library/Movies/Added.classification: jellyfin-bug-not-ported (the SELECTOR half; the refresh half is confirmed live on Ferrofin by j_library_webhooks — create by path, id-matched NFO refresh, unmatched-id negative control). Jellyfin 10.11.8 cannot match an external id on these four routes AT ALL: LibraryController.PostUpdatedSeries / PostUpdatedMovies (v10.11.8 Jellyfin.Api/Controllers/LibraryController.cs:571-635) query with `DtoOptions(false)`, whose ctor sets `Fields = []` (MediaBrowser.Controller/Dto/DtoOptions.cs:29-37), so BaseItemRepository.ApplyNavigations skips `Include(e => e.Provider)` (Jellyfin.Server.Implementations/Item/BaseItemRepository.cs:442-444) and DeserializeBaseItem never fills ProviderIds (:895-897) — the in-memory `string.Equals(id, i.GetProviderId(...))` filter therefore compares every item against null. Measured twice on the C4 lab pair 2026-08-30 (F=18296, J=18297): (a) a supplied id matches NOTHING even when the item demonstrably carries it — Jellyfin's own DTO reports Movie 0001 as ProviderIds {Imdb: tt0111161} and `POST /Library/Movies/Updated?imdbId=tt0111161` produced no `will be refreshed` line in 20 s; a probe series carrying Tvdb 990002 was still at its old Overview 60 s after `?tvdbId=990002`, and the same probe pair run through the journey leaves all four rows H=True J=False. (b) with the id OMITTED, `string.Equals(null, null)` is TRUE, so a bare `POST /Library/Series/Added` reported EVERY series (logged: the probe plus Series 01-08 'will be refreshed' in one burst) — a whole-TV-library refresh from an empty request. Ferrofin pushes the id into the SQL query instead (`paths_by_provider_id` → InternalItemsQuery::any_provider_id_equals, crates/ferrofin-api/src/handlers/library.rs), so a real id matches and an absent id is a no-op: the route's documented intent, kept under the repo's 'don't port Jellyfin bugs' rule. These rows therefore cannot be deep_verified against this oracle; the journey records Ferrofin's effect and Jellyfin's silence rather than a green.

Ferrofin pushes the id into the SQL query instead (`paths_by_provider_id` → InternalItemsQuery::any_provider_id_equals, crates/ferrofin-api/src/handlers/library.rs), so a real id matches and an absent id is a no-op: the route's documented intent, kept under the repo's 'don't port Jellyfin bugs' rule. These rows therefore cannot be deep_verified against this oracle; the journey records Ferrofin's effect and Jellyfin's silence rather than a green.

POST /Items/RemoteSearch/MusicArtist.classification: The library metadata-fetcher gate is now PORTED on this path: `LocalProviderManager::remote_search` resolves the `ItemId` reference item, reads ITS library's TypeOptions and drops every remote fetcher the "Metadata downloaders" list leaves unticked, honouring `IncludeDisabledProviders` as the short-circuit and the library's `MetadataFetcherOrder` for ordering — a port of MediaBrowser.Providers/Manager/ProviderManager.cs:787-830 -> :440-460 -> :462-491 -> MediaBrowser.Controller/BaseItemManager/BaseItemManager.cs:26-46. It only became REACHABLE for MusicArtist once `MusicArtistResolver` landed, because the gate resolves a library through `TopParentId` and an accessed-by-name artist has none. Measured live on the lab pair, both servers: scoped search with `ItemId` -> 200 with 0 results on BOTH (the fixture library ticks no MusicArtist fetcher; Ferrofin used to return 25), and `IncludeDisabledProviders=true` puts MusicBrainz back. The row also gained its first probe — `j_remote_search_identify` now sends `ItemId` and `IncludeDisabledProviders`, which no case did before, and resolves the artist id PER SERVER by Path so a server with no resolvable artist FAILS the row rather than skipping it. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT, not a divergence: MusicBrainz rate-limits both containers behind one egress IP and answers an over-rate query with an empty list, so the probe paces its legs 6 s apart and retries 5 times; if both servers still come back empty the row goes red with `named_count: 0` on both, which is the honest reading. The unscoped candidate list is compared whole, field for field, with ORDER normalised only — MusicBrainz returns tie-scored artists in an order two independent live queries do not agree on.
